sources.title: Lingyin Temple Hangzhou, Temple of the Soul's Retreat in Hangzhou
sources.content:
Lingyin Temple - Complete Text Content

Overview
Lingyin Temple, also known as the "Temple of the Soul's Retreat," is one of the largest and most visited Buddhist temples in China that houses the largest statue of the Buddha Sakyamuni in the lotus position. The temple was established in 328 AD by Indian monk Huili.

Location & Name
Chinese: 灵隐寺 Lingyin Si
Location: Fei Lai Feng Scenic Area, west of Hangzhou City
Activities: Buddhist worship, sightseeing

Legend & History
The temple earned its name from its serene location, sheltered by forested hills from three sides. Throughout history it has been damaged and undergone renovation several times and has recently been rebuilt in its original style.

Main Attractions

The Laughing Buddha
The temple contains the Hall of the Heavenly King, Hall of the Great Hero, Hall of the Buddha of Medicine, East and West Winding Corridors and several other buildings. The Hall of the Heavenly King features a statue of Maitreya, the fat, bare and bellied Buddha with a smiling face – the laughing Buddha.

Sakyamuni Statue
A 19-meter tall statue is seated on a 10.5-meter high lotus flower amidst great red pillars and murals in the Hall of the Great Hero. Behind it sits a colorful sculpture of 150 Buddhas. The temple also contains a large collection of Buddhist treasures and relics, which are significant for the development of Buddhism in the region.

500 Arhats
One more recently added hall holds 500 Arhats: bronze statues resembling 500 of the earliest high-ranking Buddhist disciples in China.

Practical Information

Admission & Hours
Entry Fee: CNY 30
Operating Hours: 7am – 6:15pm
Duration: 1 hour recommended visit

Transportation
Visitors can take special tourist buses at Hangzhou Railway (main) Train Station, for example, 1 (Y1), 2 (Y2), 7/K7, Y13, or K807/K837. The stop is called "Lingyin" and is situated 9 km away from the West Lake. Bus fares range 1-3 yuan, while a taxi will cost you CNY 10 for the first 3 kilometers, then 2-3 yuan per kilometer: that's about 15 yuan from West Lake.

Rules of Conduct
Flash photography and smoking are forbidden inside the temple, although noise (including prayers and psalms) and incense sticks are allowed everywhere.

Nearby Attractions
- Peak Flown From Afar: features ancient trees, grotesque rocks, deep caves and solemn statues of Buddha
- West Lake: the symbol of Hangzhou, considered one of the most beautiful sights in China
- Six Harmonies Pagoda: offers a fine view of Qiantang River

sources.title: 2026 Lingyin Temple Travel Guide: History, Tips & Highlights
sources.content:
Lingyin Temple Travel Guide 2026

Lingyin Temple is a sacred Buddhist site with over 1,600 years of history nestled among breathtaking landscapes, located in the West Lake area of Hangzhou.

Key Information
Location: No. 1 Fayun Alley, Lingyin Road, Xihu District, Hangzhou
Hours: Year-round: 06:30 – 18:15 (Summer)/17:45 (Winter)
Admission: CNY 75/person, including CNY 45 per person for Feilai Peak Scenic Area and CNY 30 per person for Lingyin Temple

Best Time to Visit
Visit early in the morning (before 9 AM) when the temple first opens for a more peaceful experience. Spring (March-May) is perhaps the most magical time to visit, when cherry blossoms and magnolias bloom throughout the temple grounds.

Etiquette and Rules
As an active place of worship, respectful behavior is essential—speak softly, especially in prayer halls where monks and devotees worship. Flash photography and smoking are forbidden inside the temple.

What to Experience
Lingyin Temple offers a free incense-lighting experience. After entering the temple, you can receive three incense sticks for free. Adjacent to the temple, the traditional tea house serves local Dragon Well (Longjing) tea in meditative surroundings.

Nearby Attractions
Feilai Peak features numerous fantastically shaped caves and over 340 Buddhist grotto carvings dating back to the Five Dynasties period. Nine Creeks and Eighteen Gullies is a picturesque hiking area with streams, bamboo forests, and tea plantations starting just behind Lingyin Temple. The moderate 4-5 hour trail showcases the natural beauty that inspired centuries of Chinese poets.

Starting December 1, 2025, you can enter Lingyin Temple for free, making it easier for everyone to experience the temple's beauty.

sources.title: Lingyin Temple, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China: History, Map
sources.content:
Lingyin Temple, Hangzhou

Lingyin Temple is recognized as a National Key Buddhist Temple and an important part of UNESCO World Heritage site - West Lake Cultural Landscape of Hangzhou.

Founded in 326 AD by Indian monk Huili, Lingyin Temple ("Soul's Retreat") has stood as a spiritual beacon in Hangzhou for over 1,700 years. This spot ranks as one of the top must-see attractions in Hangzhou, drawing nearly 11 million visitors every year.

You will find ancient halls, peaceful courtyards, and the famous Feilai Peak with over 340 carved grotto statues. Before entering the temples themselves, you first walk through Feilai Peak, an area filled with hundreds of Buddhist carvings dating back to the 10th century, with cliffs dotted with ancient grottoes, arhats, flying apsaras, and stories from Buddhist sutras, creating a setting that feels like an open-air museum carved into the mountain.

The best time to go is in the morning, especially during spring and autumn, where you will enjoy pleasant weather and fewer crowds. If you want to avoid crowds, try to visit on weekdays.

It is very pleasant to dine at the Lingyin Vegetarian Restaurant located nearby, where the vegetarian dishes on offer are typical of the Chinese culinary style and frequently regarded as 'food for the gods'.

sources.title: Lingyin Temple Is Now Free to Enter? Tap to Learn More
sources.content:
Lingyin Temple Free Entry Update

Starting December 1, 2025, you can enter Lingyin Temple for free, making it easier for everyone to experience the temple's beauty. Previously the admission fee was CNY 75 (including CNY 45 for Feilai Peak Scenic Area and CNY 30 for Lingyin Temple).

The new free entry policy requires advance reservation through the "杭州灵隐飞来峰" mini-program on WeChat or Alipay. Reservations can be made up to 7 days in advance, but must be made at least 1 day before your visit - same-day reservations are not accepted.

Daily capacity limits: Weekdays 35,000 visitors/day, Weekends 50,000 visitors/day, Holidays 65,000 visitors/day. Time slots: Morning (7:30-12:00) and Afternoon (12:00-17:00).

Visitors aged 70 and above are exempt from the reservation requirement.

Since February 2026, no-show penalties have been strengthened: first no-show suspends reservation privileges for 30 days, second for 60 days, third for 90 days.

sources.title: Temple of Soul's Retreat, Lingyin Temple, Hangzhou
sources.content:
Temple of Soul's Retreat, Lingyin Temple, Hangzhou

Lingyin Temple is Hangzhou's oldest renowned Buddhist temple, housing numerous exquisite cultural relics from various dynasties. Feilai Peak features numerous fantastically shaped caves and over 340 Buddhist grotto carvings dating back to the Five Dynasties period, making it a rare gem of ancient grotto art in southern China.

Gates open at 7:00 AM. Best visiting times are spring (March–May) or autumn (September–November).

By Bus: You can take Tourism Bus Y1, Y2, regular bus routes 7/K7, Y13, K807/K837 and get off at Lingyin Station.

By Taxi: Taking a taxi is more advisable, and you will reach Lingyin Temple directly within one hour.

For visitor inquiries, you can call +86-571-87968665 or +86-571-87972236.

sources.title: 灵隐寺_百度百科
sources.content:
灵隐寺完整文字内容

基本信息
灵隐寺（LingYin Temple），又名云林寺，地处浙江省杭州市西湖以西，背靠北高峰，面朝飞来峰，为杭州最早的名刹，始建于东晋咸和元年（公元326年），占地面积约87000平方米，现任方丈光泉法师。

历史沿革

东晋：灵隐寺建于东晋咸和元年（326年）。相传印度僧人慧理至此，认为飞来峰是"仙灵所隐"之地，遂面山建寺，取名"灵隐"。

五代十国：吴越王钱镠时期的摩崖石刻、佛像塑造特别丰富。后汉天福十二年（947年），吴越王钱弘仿曾扩建灵隐寺为九楼、十八阁、七十二殿。僧众三千之多。

北宋：宋真宗景德四年（1007年），改灵隐寺为灵隐山景德寺。天圣八年（1030年），因灵隐寺斋僧施粥的需要，将杭州、秀州两地良田一万三千余亩赐与灵隐寺作为庙产。

南宋：绍兴五年（1135年），将灵隐寺改为"灵隐寺崇恩显亲禅寺"。高宗和孝宗时常到灵隐寺进香。

清：清康熙二十八年（1689年），康熙帝南巡杭州时驾幸灵隐寺。康熙亲书"云林"二字，灵隐寺遂改名为"云林禅寺"。乾隆帝六次驾幸灵隐，都留有诗文刊刻于石。

建国后：1952年由政府拨款修复大殿。1975年经国务院批准全面整修，共耗资130余万元。

建筑格局
灵隐寺布局与江南寺院格局大致相仿，全寺建筑中轴线上依次为天王殿、大雄宝殿、药师殿三大殿。总体规划沿中轴线形成五层格局：天王殿-大雄宝殿-药师殿-藏经楼-华严殿。

主要景点

飞来峰：作为禅宗五山之首，飞来峰石刻造像是中国南方石窟艺术的重要作品，470多尊造像中保存完整和比较完整的有335尊。最为人所知的是大肚弥勒和18罗汉群像，此为飞来峰摩崖石刻中最大的造像，也是国内最早的大肚弥勒造像。

天王殿：长约24米，宽约15米。正中面朝山门的佛龛供奉弥勒佛像。背对山门的佛龛供奉韦驮雕像，以香樟木雕造，是南宋留存至今的珍贵遗物，已有700多年历史。天王殿上悬"云林禅寺"匾额，为清康熙帝所题。

大雄宝殿：原称觉皇殿，重檐高33.6米。正中释迦牟尼莲花坐像高24.8米，是中国最高大的香樟木坐式佛像之一。殿后有"慈航普渡"、"五十三参"海岛立体群塑，共有佛像150尊。

药师殿：供奉"东方三圣"：药师佛及日光天子、月光天子。

灵隐铜殿：高达12.62米，为中华第一高铜殿，获世界吉尼斯最高铜殿纪录。

旅游贴士
开放时间：07:00~18:15。佛诞节日、朔望、国定节假日早上提前30分钟开门。

门票：2025年12月1日起，灵隐飞来峰景区（含灵隐寺、永福寺、韬光寺）实行免票政策。原票价：飞来峰45元，灵隐寺30元。须先购买飞来峰景区门票才能进入灵隐寺。早上05:30以前进入飞来峰景区免票。

预约制度：自2025年12月1日起实行"实名预约、分时游览"。预约量：工作日3.5万人次/天、双休日5万人次/天、节假日6.5万人次/天。按上午（7:30-12:00）、下午（12:00-17:00）两个时段分段预约。70周岁(含)以上免预约入园。

2026年2月1日起优化升级：全面推行"线上候补"功能，首次爽约暂停预约资格30日，第二次60日，第三次90日。

交通：杭州公交7路（灵隐公交总站至城站火车站）、505路、278路、319路等可达。龙翔桥至灵隐专线、武林广场至灵隐专线等专线也可到达。

寺庙传说
飞来峰传说：济公和尚算知有一座山峰就要从远处飞来，怕压死村民就冲进一户娶新娘的人家背起新娘子就跑，村人追出后山峰飞降压没了整个村庄。
康熙题匾：康熙皇帝写了个大"雨"字后发现"灵"字笔画太多摆不下，在随从暗示下将错就错写成"云林禅寺"。

sources.title: 2026杭州灵隐寺游玩攻略(时间地点+门票政策)
sources.content:
2026杭州灵隐寺游玩攻略

自2025年12月1日起，灵隐飞来峰景区（含灵隐寺、永福寺、韬光寺）实行免票政策。之前的门票价格为灵隐寺门票75元（含飞来峰景区门票45元，灵隐寺香火券30元）。

预约方式：通过手机上的支付宝或微信平台，搜索"杭州灵隐飞来峰"小程序，进行实名预约，可以提前预约未来7天的名额。预约至少提前1天，不接受当日预约。

开放时间：每日7:30-17:30（17:00停止入园）。

灵隐寺始建于东晋咸和元年（公元326年），至今已有约一千七百年的历史，为杭州最早的名刹。灵隐寺地处杭州西湖以西，背靠北高峰，面朝飞来峰。主要由天王殿、大雄宝殿、药师殿、直指堂（法堂）、华严殿为中轴线，两边附以五百罗汉堂、济公殿、联灯阁、华严阁、大悲楼、方丈楼等建筑所构成，共占地一百三十亩。

sources.title: Travelogue: The Top Tier. Hangzhou's Lingyin Temple
sources.content:
Travelogue: The Top Tier - Hangzhou's Lingyin Temple

Lingyin Temple offers visitors experiences such as tracing the footsteps of poet-governor Bai Juyi (9th century), studying Song Dynasty wood architecture, participating in monastic daily rituals, and meditating along the "Path of Enlightenment" lined with 500 arhat statues.

Before entering the temples themselves, you first walk through Feilai Peak, an area filled with hundreds of Buddhist carvings dating back to the 10th century, with cliffs dotted with ancient grottoes, arhats, flying apsaras, and stories from Buddhist sutras, creating a setting that feels like an open-air museum carved into the mountain.

The temple draws nearly 11 million visitors every year, making it one of China's most visited Buddhist sites.
